question.text: The product of all the rational roots of the equation $\left(x^2-9 x+11\right)^2-(x-4)(x-5)=3$, is equal to

solution.text:
$\begin{aligned}
& \left(x^2-9 x+11\right)^2-(x-4)(x-5)=3 \\
& \left(x^2-9 x+11\right)^2-\left(x^2-9 x+20\right)=3
\end{aligned}$
Let $x^2-9 x+11=t$
$\begin{aligned}
& t^2-(t+9)=3 \\
& \Rightarrow t^2-t-12=0 \\
& \Rightarrow t^2-4 t+3 t-12=0 \\
& \Rightarrow t(t-4)+3(t-4)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow t=4 \text { or }-3 \\
& x^2-9 x+11=4 \\
& x^2-9 x+7=0
\end{aligned}$
Here, we will get irrational roots
$\begin{aligned}
& x^2-9 x+11=-3 \\
& x^2-9 x+14=0 \\
& x^2-7 x-2 x+14=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x=7,2 \\
& \Rightarrow \text { Product of all rational roots }=14
\end{aligned}$
